title: SOCOM U.S. Navy SEALs: Fireteam Bravo
subtitle: A tactical squad travels onto PSP

body: SOCOM U.S. Navy SEALs: Fireteam Bravo is Zipper Interactive's portable tactical shooter, first released in North America on 8 November 2005. It brings the SOCOM approach to PSP through a third-person campaign and wireless multiplayer. The player enters missions with military equipment and the need to recognise threats before committing to an approach. Moving onto a handheld also required changes to the familiar console controls. The result places the series' interest in armed teamwork within a machine whose single analogue nub cannot reproduce the controller layout of the PlayStation 2 games directly.

Holding the right shoulder button locks onto a target before firing, allowing the player to manage movement without a second analogue stick dedicated to aiming. Sniper rifles, assault rifles, machine guns and grenades provide different responses to the mission. The choice of equipment matters alongside identifying a target, since distance and the surrounding threats can make one approach more useful than another. Fireteam Bravo retains the need to read an encounter while adapting the physical act of aiming to PSP, making the hardware limitation part of the design rather than simply copying the larger console's controls.

The game supports both local ad-hoc connections between PSP systems and infrastructure play through a wireless network. Up to sixteen players could compete online, with voice chat helping bring the series' communication-focused identity onto the handheld. Reviews were generally positive, and Fireteam Bravo became a portable branch of SOCOM with further sequels. Official online servers closed in 2012. Its original significance lies in the ambition of the package: a handheld tactical campaign accompanied by a substantial networked game, offered at a time when console-style online features were becoming increasingly important to portable systems.
